title: Geometry-encoded deep learning (GeoDL) framework for real-time 3D dose verification for online adaptive radiotherapy.
summary: A geometry-encoded 3D U-Net estimates dose from integrated fluence maps and CT volumes; 281 prostate cases were used for training/validation and 24 separate cases for testing against treatment-planning dose. Reported agreement and speed support a retrospective dosimetric feasibility result; use remains limited to prostate VMAT/single LINAC configuration, with clinical implementation still future work.
ai_technology: A geometry-encoded CT/fluence-map input is processed by 3D U-Net to estimate full-volume dose.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: 281 prostate cases used for training/validation and 24 separate test cases compared against TPS calculations; single site/VMAT/LINAC limits remain.
evidence.unknown: External replication and real-world or clinical benefit were not established by the reviewed study; author affiliation is not stated in the reviewed material.
